findings.title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of what its name claims
findings.description: The test is named to check that a processing error does not block offset commits for other messages. Offset 100 raises and offset 101 succeeds. Both offsets are completed in the worker's `finally` block, so the tracker should eventually commit 102. The final assertion is `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which asserts that no commit happened. The commit loop waits about one second before its first pass, and the test only waits about 0.2s after processing finishes. So the assertion can pass without any commit ever occurring. The test does not check the behavior its name describes.

findings.title: Racy assertion on total_items immediately after submit
findings.description: The test submits 10 items and then asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0` straight away. Worker threads are already consuming from the queues, so the queues may be empty by the time `get_stats()` runs. That makes the assertion timing-dependent and likely to flake.

findings.title: Helper method may not exist on the new Kafka test base class
findings.description: The new class `ProcessResultThreadQueueParallelKafkaTest` inherits from `UptimeTestCase`, but its test calls `self.create_uptime_result(...)`. In this diff, that helper is used by the `ProcessResultTest` hierarchy. I could not confirm that `UptimeTestCase` defines it. If it does not, the Kafka test fails with an AttributeError before it reaches any Kafka logic.

findings.title: Topic deletion result is never checked and exceptions are swallowed
findings.description: In the `finally` block, `admin_client.delete_topics([test_topic])` is called without using the returned futures. Kafka admin errors are reported through those futures, so the call never surfaces a failure. The surrounding `except Exception: pass` then hides any exception raised synchronously. The test can leak topics without any signal.
